text: Your video call freezes for four seconds. Annoying. For a robot goalkeeper? Maybe fatal.
Last time, an overhead camera rescued our duck from a blocked view. But we'd quietly assumed its pixels arrived on time.
So we froze the robot, the shots, the physics, and the predictor. Then we delayed the camera feed.
No lag: fifteen saves out of fifteen. One second: still fifteen. Two seconds: somehow, still fifteen.
At three seconds, it just clears our bar: twelve out of fifteen.
Then four seconds. The frames do arrive, with their original timestamps, but the duck gets the message after the moment is gone. Seven saves out of fifteen.
Great. We found the cliff. Next, the Wi-Fi starts dropping frames.
